body.estimand_functional: For every admissible degree sequence, a universal deterministic certified upper edge satisfies \(R(G)\le C d_n^2/n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\) and every simple \(d_n\)-regular \(G\), attained by the graph-auditable selected one-shot seed procedure. Under the uniform simple random-regular draw, \(\Pr\{R(G_n)\ge c d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\}\to1\), and the joint high-probability bracket follows. Bounded degree gives \(R(G_n)=\Theta_{\Pr}(n^{-1})\); when \(d_n\to\infty\), a factor \(\log(d_n+1)\) remains between the proved edges.

sampling_model.design: The graph \(G=G_n\) is revealed first.  On \(M_n<n\), the experimenter fixes \(c_0\in(0,1)\), computes the robust candidate \(\widetilde k_n=\max\{1,\lfloor c_0/[-\log(1-M_n/n)]\rfloor\}\) and the log-tuned candidate \(k_n^\sharp=\max\{1,\lfloor\log(d_n+1)/[4\{-\log(1-M_n/n)\}]\rfloor\}\), and chooses the candidate with smaller graph certificate before drawing seeds.  It then treats the union of the selected number of uniform seeds' closed neighborhoods.  The finite fallback assigns every unit treatment when the positive-exposure branch is unavailable or the selected certificate exceeds one.
sampling_model.units: The population \(V_n\) and every potential outcome are fixed conditional on \(G\). The graph is random only for the high-probability frontier statement.
sampling_model.treatment: Exactly one binary assignment \(Z\) is drawn and all realized outcomes are observed. Seed multiplicities are integrated out of the estimator by conditional Rao--Blackwell weights.
sampling_model.overlap: No unit-level Bernoulli overlap is imposed. The seed branch is entered only when \(M_n<n\), where all endpoint exposure probabilities used in ratios are graph-computable and positive. When \(M_n\ge n\), the compiler forms no inverse-probability quantity and returns the all-treated fallback.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None. Intermediate-exposure potential outcomes are unrestricted and ignored; no prior outcomes, repeated rounds, endpoint means, behavioral model, or superpopulation outcome law is used.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Corollary 5.4 gives \(d/n\lesssim\mathcal R(G,\tau_{\mathrm{GATE}},2)\lesssim d^2/n\) with high probability for random \(d\)-regular \(G\) and \(d=o(\sqrt n)\).
Theorem 4.1 bounds the modified Horvitz--Thompson variance by \(12.5\lambda(\mathcal H)/n\) times the sum of endpoint empirical second moments.
Algorithm 4 is the paper's polynomial approximation design, Proposition 4.3 states its guarantee, and Theorem C.11 is the imported 2-approximation for Partial Vertex Cover used as a subroutine.
Theorem 4.8 bounds GATE Horvitz--Thompson variance for randomized one-hop-max clustering under bounded outcomes and restricted growth.
The paper characterizes admissible estimable quadratic variance bounds and gives convex programs selecting minimally conservative bounds for linear estimators.

body.tldr: For every admissible degree sequence and all sufficiently large \(n\), the graph-selected one-shot seed procedure gives the deterministic certified upper edge \(R(G)\le C d_n^2/n\) on every simple \(d_n\)-regular graph \(G\). Under the uniform simple random-regular draw, the balanced-exposure converse gives \(R(G_n)\ge c d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\) with probability tending to one, so the joint bracket is a corollary. Bounded degrees yield \(R(G_n)=\Theta_{\Pr}(n^{-1})\); diverging degrees leave a factor \(\log(d_n+1)\) between the proved edges. The selected procedure also gives finite conditional coverage and unconditional radius \(O(d_n/\sqrt{\alpha n})=o(1)\) for fixed \(\alpha\). A sharper logarithmic upper edge and radius remain conditional on the unresolved Boolean radius-two operator conjecture.

project_justification.gap: On the common uniform-simple-regular regime \(d_n=o(\sqrt n)\), KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax gives the same \(d_n^2/n\) upper scale and a \(d_n/n\) lower scale for exactly the same two-endpoint outcome class and minimax functional. The present all-procedure lower edge is \(d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\), reducing the polynomial factor-\(d_n\) gap to a factor \(\log(d_n+1)\); equality with the lower edge remains open.
project_justification.niche: Balanced simultaneous endpoint exposure supplies a two-arm Bayes converse, while certificate-based selection between fixed-exponent and log-tuned neighborhood-seed counts makes the exact Schur construction robust without discarding a possible sharper rate.
project_justification.fill: The note proves a deterministic certified upper edge on every sufficiently large simple regular graph by inserting the robust candidate into the exact selected seed/Schur certificate and then using that procedure as a feasible competitor in the minimax infimum. Separately, balanced simultaneous endpoint exposure and the Bayes converse give the random-regular lower edge over every design and estimator. Their conjunction yields the high-probability logarithmic bracket, while exact seed-tuple enumeration supplies a finite graph audit and the risk certificate yields the stated design-based confidence guarantee. The Boolean operator conjecture is retained only as a conditional refinement.

body.related_work: KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax, arXiv:2608.04909v1, Corollary 5.4 and Appendix E.4, is the closest comparator. On the common uniform-simple-regular regime \(d_n=o(\sqrt n)\), its \(q=2\) GATE outcome class and minimax functional coincide exactly with this note's \(\mathcal M_n(G)\) and \(R(G)\); this is equality of the compared problem, not a class-inclusion transfer. It places that risk between \(d_n/n\) and \(d_n^2/n\). The present balanced-exposure converse improves the lower edge to \(d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\), while the selected seed certificate provides a deterministic, graph-auditable upper edge at the same \(d_n^2/n\) order, leaving a logarithmic gap. Its Algorithm 4 and Proposition 4.3 motivate finite design computation but do not give this selected seed certificate. KandirosEtAl2024ConflictGraph, arXiv:2411.10908v3, Algorithm 1 and Theorem 4.1, supplies a generic conflict-graph variance scale; the current unconditional upper edge does not strictly improve that scale. UganderYin2023RGCR studies randomized graph cluster designs under bounded outcomes and a fixed Horvitz--Thompson procedure, rather than unrestricted minimax risk. AronowSamii2017GeneralInterference supplies the exposure-mapping foundation. BehagueIlkovicMontgomery2025Sandwich supports the proved random-regular packing transfer in its verified degree regime. Xu2025SwitchingGraphMatrices, CCC 2025 Theorems 14--15, treats graph-matrix shapes but does not uniformly resum the unbounded \(K_{2,r}\)-type terms in the Boolean inclusion--exclusion expansion. BauerschmidtEtAl2020EdgeRigidity and Sarid2023SpectralGap control adjacency spectra, not this Boolean correction. HarshawMiddletonSavje2026OptimizedVariance optimizes conservative bounds for fixed linear estimators and does not choose the minimax design. ShiEtAl2020FreedomChoice remains the prospective application: a larger one-round all-free versus all-fixed random-regular public-goods experiment can use the robust certificate without assuming its behavioral outcomes attain worst-case risk.
body.technical_internal_limitation: For \(i\ne j\), let \(c_{ij}=(A_G^2)_{ij}\).  The exact identity is \(B_2(G)_{ij}=A_{G,ij}+(1-A_{G,ij})\sum_{r=1}^{d_n}(-1)^{r+1}\binom{c_{ij}}r\), with \(B_2(G)_{ii}=1\).  The unresolved conjecture is that some universal \(L<\infty\) satisfies \(\Pr\{\|B_2(G_n)P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le Ld_n^{7/4}\}\to1\) uniformly over every admissible degree sequence.  Xu2025SwitchingGraphMatrices, CCC 2025 Theorems 14--15, does not by itself uniformly resum these unbounded \(K_{2,r}\)-type shapes.  Accordingly the conjecture is not a premise of the unconditional risk or confidence theorem; it yields only the separately labeled logarithmic refinement.
body.honest_scope: The established result consists of a deterministic certified upper edge and a random-regular lower edge, with their joint logarithmic bracket as a corollary; it is not a matched frontier. For every admissible sequence, the selected robust seed candidate gives \(R(G)\le C d_n^2/n\) on every sufficiently large simple \(d_n\)-regular graph. The balanced-packing argument gives \(R(G_n)\ge c d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\) with high probability over the uniform graph and uniformly over all procedures. Thus bounded degree has order \(n^{-1}\), while diverging degree retains a logarithmic gap. The Boolean operator estimate remains an explicit conjecture and yields only a conditional sharper edge. Seed probabilities and inverse weights are formed only on \(M_n<n\); the complementary branch uses an all-treated fallback. The result concerns one assignment, unrestricted intermediate ANI outcomes, and the full population GATE. It does not cover later strategic feedback, final wealth, two-hop individual payoff, repeated experiments, nonuniform graph draws, or a claim that the ShiEtAl2020FreedomChoice behavioral model is worst case.
